chunks: "LiDAR's value is direct, accurate 3D geometry that doesn't depend on ambient light, so it shows up wherever machines need to know the shape of the world.
The famous one is autonomous driving and driver assistance: detecting vehicles, pedestrians and road edges at 100 to 250 meters, in the dark, with centimeter-level range.
Then robotics: warehouse robots, delivery robots and robot vacuums use 2D or 3D LiDAR for mapping and localization, and for safety scanners that stop a machine when someone enters a zone.

In surveying and mapping, airborne LiDAR flies over terrain and forests and gives you ground elevation under the trees from the last returns, and terrestrial scanners capture buildings, construction progress and archaeological sites.
Drones use small LiDARs for obstacle avoidance and inspection of power lines.
On the consumer side, phones and tablets have small time-of-flight depth sensors for autofocus, portrait effects and AR room scanning.
Other uses include wind and atmospheric sensing with Doppler LiDAR, bathymetric LiDAR with green lasers for shallow seabeds, and even speed or traffic monitoring.

A highway car needs long range and a narrow forward field of view; a robot vacuum wants cheap, short range 360°; a mapping drone cares about point density and accuracy; a phone wants tiny, low power and eye safe."
